attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, written in the first person and endorsed. He is not quoting or paraphrasing anyone else.

semantics.note: The core claim, that LLMs lack reliability, is firm. The link to the ROI studies is hedged ('seems to bear that out'), and the normalised wording keeps that hedge with 'appear to confirm'. Treating it as an observation is right.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and allows for the tentative link. It does not require exclusive causation. However, Marcus named no studies and no reliability measure, so the evaluator's choice of studies, the current-year window, and the corroboration standard all decide the result.

evidence.note: An Aug 2026 preprint with a controlled study shows LLM agents become unreliable on long workflows. This supports the reliability part only; it does not measure ROI.

A Teradata disclosure of a commissioned survey (fieldwork Mar–Apr 2026). 63% of respondents report at most small or emerging returns from agentic AI, and 51% cite output reliability as a barrier. This is partial corroboration, and the disclosure blames data foundations as the main cause.
An EY disclosure: 16% of companies report zero ROI and 43% report returns above 50%. EY blames timing, readiness, and economics, not specifically reliability. Fieldwork dates are not given.
A Deloitte disclosure dated Oct 2026. It covers AI broadly, reports revenue gains and organisational bottlenecks, and neither confirms nor refutes the reliability-to-ROI link.

reviews.rationale: e1 and e2 support the claim that LLMs lack reliability. But only one survey (e2, a company-commissioned one) both reports limited returns and names reliability as a barrier, and even that survey blames data problems first. EY and Deloitte (e3, e4) show mixed or positive returns and point to other causes. The support condition, several studies tying return shortfalls to reliability, is not met. Nothing establishes dependable performance or refutes the link either, so the packet does not settle the claim.
